title: Toolchain: MPI, CUDA toolkit, compilers
done_when: mpicxx --version, nvcc --version and nvidia-smi all work
outcome: Done on the HPC system instead of WSL: NVIDIA HPC SDK 25.11 (nvcc 13.0, HPC-X Open MPI 4.1.9 with CUDA support), mpicxx wrapping GCC 11.5 (scripts/env.sh)

title: First compile and make check (OpenMP backend, 16^3, 2 ranks)
done_when: make all builds with no errors and make check prints PASS; mpirun -np 8 ./bin/halo3d_omp --n 16 --steps 50 also PASSes (exercises x and y faces)
outcome: Compiled first time with no warnings (-Wall -Wextra); make check PASS (4.4e-15); 8 and 12 ranks, n = 16, 17, 23 PASS (results/check.csv)

title: CUDA backend correctness
done_when: --backend cuda PASSes for np = 1, 2, 4 and for --n 17 (uneven split); errors match the omp backend to round-off
outcome: np = 1, 2, 4 (4 = two nodes), n = 16, 17, 64, host-staged and CUDA-aware: all PASS with errors identical to the omp backend (results/check.csv, 24/24)

title: Single-node performance sweep with measured bandwidth roofs
done_when: thread scaling, ranks x threads, STREAM-style CPU and GPU copy bandwidth in results/; roofline uses the measured roof
outcome: CPU node 8.30 GLUP/s = 92% of the 145 GB/s copy roof (after the y-blocking fix); A100 81.8 GLUP/s, interior kernel 79% of the 1653 GB/s copy roof

title: Profile overlap and tune the interior kernel
done_when: an Nsight Systems timeline shows the interior kernel overlapping pack/copy/MPI; Nsight Compute DRAM throughput recorded; BX/BY/KZ choice justified in README
outcome: Overlap measured from timers instead (whole step vs interior kernel vs MPI wait, results/breakdown_*.png); found and fixed the stream-priority starvation bug. Not done: Nsight timeline, Nsight Compute, BX/BY/KZ sweep

title: Publish the repo with measured numbers
done_when: public GitHub repo; README results table has measured rows only, compile-tested line updated
outcome: README rewritten from the CSVs; site names removed from scripts and logs; publishing is handled separately

title: GPU strong scaling on 1-16 GPUs (host staging)
outcome: A100 80GB PCIe, N = 1024: P = 1..16, 3 runs each, all PASS (results/gpu_strong.csv)

title: GPU weak scaling on 1-16 GPUs
done_when: results/gpu_weak.csv holds P = 1..16, all PASS; weak-efficiency plot committed
outcome: L = 512 and L = 1024 per GPU, P = 1..16, all PASS (results/gpu_weak.csv, results/gpu_weak_L1024.csv, results/scaling.png)

title: CUDA-aware MPI vs host staging
done_when: if ompi_info reports CUDA support: strong/weak rerun with --cuda-aware and wait_s compared in README
outcome: mpi_built_with_cuda_support = true; CUDA-aware is slower across nodes on this machine because the NIC sits on the other socket from the GPUs (OSU: 4.1 GB/s device-to-device vs 12.1 GB/s host-to-host)

title: CPU (OpenMP backend) strong and weak scaling
done_when: strong and weak CSVs for the omp backend (one rank per socket) committed with plots
outcome: 1..16 nodes, 2 ranks/node x 24 threads: strong 1024^3 86% efficiency, weak 512^3/rank 90% (results/cpu_strong.csv, results/cpu_weak.csv)

title: Write-up: scaling analysis and resume bullet from measured numbers
done_when: README explains where efficiency drops and why, every number in the table traces to a committed CSV; one resume bullet drafted from those numbers
outcome: README analysis + bugs section; notes/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md (private study guide) has the interview prep
